chapter: New Orleans and the tent shows
title: Pete Lala's, a theater built for Billy, and young Armstrong
summary: They place Pete Lala's cabaret and a little theater built for Billy near Claiborne and Conti. Mary recalls Louis Armstrong sneaking out of the home for boys to play with Oliver at night.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well, this place of Pete Lawless, was that the one at Marais and the Custom House? Yes, yes. I think Professor Minetta said he opened another place back on Villery someplace.
Villery, well that was a little theater.
He built for me. Oh, really? I didn't know about that. It was in a theater.
That was a little theater. Uh-huh. Really?
Yes. Where was that just about? On Claiborne, between the basin, the old basin up there, the new basin. That's the old basin.
We're about in, I know about where it is.
Yeah. It's not there now, of course. There's a cemetery in there, of course. Oh, that was across the street.
Across the street from the theater. From the theater. Or rather, the theater was built across the street from the cemetery.

And Louis Armstrong, he was out to Miss Joseph's home. That was a home for bad boys. Yes, I remember. And then he would come to the cabaret at night and put on long pants and play with Joe in there, with sneaking plays. Uh-huh.
